brief: Tech sold off last week with a Friday vol spike. US and NDX outperform with some respite this morning, while EU unwinds as Russia/Ukraine tensions escalate (Trump waived energy sanctions and struck a diesel deal with Russia, pushing oil lower) and France sees fiscal protests, hitting EUR. Lower yields reflect either risk-off safe haven rotation or reduced Tech/capex yield pressure (evidenced by CoreWeave), alongside a reversal of early-October extreme short positioning. Positioning Intel flags multi-strat de-grossing near a 2-year worst despite neutral aggregate positioning, because crowded skews and high gross (Tech flows near multi-year highs, NDX long vs RTY short futures skews extreme) persist underneath. JPM is tactically bullish on global equities, preferring US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) over Europe, since Europe needs EGB-spread stability before its earnings and positioning buy signal can drive broadening. Credit strategists call hyperscaler spread widening overdone, since the $117bn YTD debt increase came with only modestly worse ratings, pointing to a selection/dispersion trade rather than indiscriminate de-risking.
